Synopsis:
The article argues that Australia's datacentre power debate — federal government pushing 100% renewable requirements vs. state governments favouring gas/coal — reveals a deeper structural problem: renewables and grid infrastructure are not being built fast enough to meet growing electricity demand. Datacentres represent only 17% of future demand growth; EVs, electrification and population growth make up the rest. The author, from the Grattan Institute, calls for binding emissions restrictions on electricity generators and faster infrastructure permitting as the real solutions.
